strategy_hint_title: How your retirement spending responds to how the portfolio actually performs.
strategy_fixed_title: Spend the same amount every year, adjusted for inflation. Simple, but ignores market performance.
strategy_guardrails_title: Simplified withdrawal-rate guardrails inspired by Guyton-Klinger: trim spending when the withdrawal rate rises beyond its band, and raise it when the rate falls below the band.
strategy_percent_of_portfolio_title: Recalculate portfolio-funded spending annually from the current balance. Spending adapts, but the floor, market losses, taxes, and other outflows mean the portfolio can still run out.
note_strategy_guardrails: Cuts or raises spending by the adjustment step whenever your withdrawal rate drifts past the band from its starting level. Spending stays within {floor}–{ceiling} of your planned amount.
note_strategy_percent: Spends this share of the current balance each year, clamped to {floor}–{ceiling} of your planned amount so income never collapses or balloons.
note_strategy_fixed: Keeps planned real spending unchanged regardless of portfolio performance — the conventional assumption behind fixed-withdrawal analyses such as the “4% rule”.
assumptions_summary_tail: · {fees} fees · {tax} tax — open to customize the model
historical_data_available_label: Data available to both Historical modes:
historical_methodology: This dataset supplies return sequences to both Historical modes; Parametric mode does not use them. Equity returns are estimated monthly total-return proxies from Stooq price indices, with synthetic dividends where needed and foreign World indices converted to USD. Bonds use synthetic 10Y total returns from yield change plus carry; bank/cash uses short-rate proxies. Unadjusted Historical mode jointly replays CPI and returns from the same months. Adjusted Historical and Parametric modes use modelled inflation. Sources:
mode_historical_sampling_title: Replays real market history. Stitches together runs of actual past months in their original order. Returns and inflation are taken from the same real months, so the two stay linked. Averages match history and cannot be edited — the table below is read-only in this mode.
mode_historical_adjusted_title: The same real market history, rescaled to return targets you choose. Keeps history's shape — the crashes, recoveries and clustering — while sliding average return and volatility to your numbers. Use it to ask 'what if returns are worse than the past?'. Trade-off: inflation reverts to a modelled draw, so the return/inflation link is lost.
mode_parametric_title: Uses no historical data. Returns are generated from a statistical model built only from the numbers you enter, via a two-state growth/crisis regime switcher with fat-tailed draws. Most flexible and least anchored to reality — for exploring hypothetical markets rather than planning against history.
context_parametric_rest: Returns are generated from a statistical model built only from the numbers you enter below. Most flexible, least anchored to what markets actually did.
context_adjusted_strong: Real history, rescaled to your targets.
context_adjusted_rest: Keeps the shape of history — the crashes, recoveries and clustering — but slides average return and volatility to the values you set below. Answers “what if returns are worse than the past?”. Inflation falls back to a modelled draw in this mode.
context_historical_rest: Stitches together runs of actual past months in their original order. Returns and inflation come from the same real months, so high-inflation periods land on the markets that truly accompanied them. Averages match history, so the table below is read-only.
btn_use_current_yields_title: Use the latest yields embedded in this dataset plus the historical equity risk premium as editable return assumptions. These are dated observations, not live market data.
joint_inflation_title: Each simulated month draws its return and its inflation from the same real historical month, so high-inflation periods land on the same months as weak markets — and inflation keeps its real-world persistence.
joint_inflation_text: ✓ Inflation sampled jointly with returns from history
th_arith_input_title: The arithmetic mean is the mathematical center used to generate random Monte Carlo paths.
th_cagr_title: Expected Compound Annual Growth Rate (Geometric Mean). Growth over time is dragged down by volatility: CAGR ≈ Arithmetic Mean - Volatility²/2
row_tax_drag_title: Applied once a year to positive real mark-to-market investment gains (losses untaxed), whether or not assets are sold.
tax_caveat_short: It is a rough drag on returns, not a tax estimate.
tax_caveat_long: It is one flat rate charged every year on that year's gains, whether or not you sold anything — closer to an annual mark-to-market return tax than to capital gains tax. It is charged on the real (inflation-adjusted) gain, while most tax systems tax the nominal gain, so high-inflation paths are taxed too lightly. There are no account types: no ISA, 401(k), IRA, Roth, SIPP or Box 3, no tax-free allowances, no withdrawal ordering between accounts, and no required minimum distributions. Treat it as a rough drag on returns, not as your tax bill — if your savings are mostly in tax-sheltered accounts, a lower rate is usually the better approximation.
cdf_caption: Real return cumulative probability (68% and 95% ranges shaded)
label_block_length: Historical replay length (bootstrap block length, months)
block_length_title: How many consecutive real months are replayed before jumping elsewhere in history. Longer blocks preserve longer historical runs; shorter blocks preserve only short-run dependence. Six months is provisional: Politis-White is a short-block diagnostic, not a retirement-path optimum.
block_length_note_lead: Consecutive real months replayed before jumping elsewhere in history.
block_length_note_strong: The main lever on how long historical runs remain intact.
block_length_note_tail: Six months is provisional; Politis-White supports short blocks for variance estimation, not a unique retirement-path optimum.
crisis_inflation_jump_title: How much higher inflation runs during a simulated crisis than in calm periods. This only bites when inflation is modelled rather than taken from history — Parametric mode, or Historical (with Adjustments). In plain Historical Data Sampling it does nothing, because inflation is read from the same real month as the return.
crisis_inflation_no_effect_strong: No effect in the current mode
crisis_inflation_no_effect_tail: — inflation is being read from real history rather than modelled.
crisis_inflation_active: Active in this mode, because inflation is modelled rather than read from history.
random_seed_note: Leave blank for a fresh random seed each run. Set a value to reproduce an exact result — the seed actually used is shown after each run completes.
verdict_sentence_tail: estimated chance your plan stays funded through age {age}
verdict_boundary_note: Near the {percent}% rating boundary; simulation noise could place the estimate on either side.
row_typical_depletion_age: If a simulation falls short, typical depletion age
row_unfunded_spending: Planned spending left unfunded in those cases
caption_tested_adjustments: Tested adjustments likely to reach the {percent}% region
combined_note_strong: A tested adjustment likely to reach the {percent}% region:
combined_note_rest: spend {reduction}% less and retire at age {age}.
best_scenario_lead: The strongest tested adjustment is estimated at
capital_sentence_today: estimated capital needed today to stay funded in {percent}% of retirement-path replays.
capital_sentence_at_retirement: estimated capital needed at retirement to stay funded in {percent}% of retirement-path replays.
capital_card_note: The target starts every retirement replay with the same capital. Projected balances vary with accumulation outcomes, so this comparison supports but does not determine the overall success rate in the first card.
diagnostics_intro: Spending capacity, sequence-risk exposure, sampling precision, and the return distribution this run actually produced. Hidden by default because these figures support — not replace — the assessment above.
diag_capacity_capped: The plan still clears the goal at the highest spending level this sweep tests, so its real capacity at age {age} is somewhere above this figure.
diag_capacity_note: Highest tested spending level that still clears the goal at age {age}. Resolution is limited to the tested levels listed below.
diag_capacity_none: No tested spending level cleared the goal at age {age}, so a sustainable figure cannot be reported from this sweep.
diag_rule_note: The {rule} divides spending by the selected withdrawal rate, net of other income. It ignores sequence risk and your actual horizon, so where the two targets disagree, the simulated one is the one the assessment uses.
diag_sequence_note: Ruin probability spans {points} percentage points between the worst and best early-return groups. A wide spread means early retirement returns materially affect the result. Compare adaptive spending or a higher bank allocation in separate runs.
diag_sequence_unavailable: Sequence-risk buckets are unavailable for this run.
diag_sampling_noise: Monte Carlo noise: ±{value} percentage points (approximate 95% run-to-run range; {count} paths).
diag_historical_robustness: Historical robustness is not measured: this run uses one regional record with {months} months, or about {chunks} non-overlapping {blockLength}-month runs. Compare other regions, periods, and replay lengths.
diag_model_robustness: Model robustness is not measured. Vary return, inflation, and model assumptions before relying on the headline probability.
diag_distribution_note: Only mean and volatility are matched to the inputs. Skew and kurtosis emerge from the regime mixture and source data, so they need not match requested shape values.
diag_sensitivity_noise: Each sensitivity cell replays {count} paths and has up to ±{margin} percentage points of sampling noise. Cells share paths, so nearby differences are steadier than their individual margins suggest.
diag_sensitivity_scope: Recommendations are reported only from this tested range. The calculator does not extrapolate a larger spending cut or later retirement age when the goal remains outside it.
chart_timeline_note: Fan shows the middle 50% and 80% of outcomes; the thin red P5 line marks the downside level only 5% of balances fall below at each age. Dotted vertical = retirement; red dashed = simulation target; orange dotted = {rule}. Percentiles are month-by-month summaries, not individual paths.
chart_surface_title_spending_only: How spending changes the chance of staying funded to age {age}
chart_surface_title_full: How retirement timing and spending change the chance of staying funded to age {age}
surface_hover_full:
Retire at age {x}
Spending change {y}%
Estimated chance funded {p}
surface_explainer: Arrows show tested changes from your plan. The dark-green line marks the 95% goal.
surface_noise_title: Each cell replays the same stored set of simulated market paths against that cell's retirement age and spending level. Because every cell reuses the same paths, differences between neighbouring cells are more reliable than each cell's own margin suggests.
surface_noise_note: Each grid point replays {count} paths (up to ±{margin}% sampling noise). Read the pattern, not a single percentage.
sequence_chart_summary: How much does the timing of market gains and losses matter?
sequence_chart_explainer: This groups simulations by returns during the first ten years after retirement. Early losses can do more damage because withdrawals leave less invested for a recovery. This is often called sequence risk.
